fields.description_1:
Kervana serves homeowners who may know they have a heating or climate problem without knowing which technical service they need. Heating, cooling, maintenance and installation questions can overlap, especially when an existing system is involved. The first task was therefore to make those routes understandable without asking visitors to diagnose the problem themselves.

The site also needed to keep practical information close to the relevant service and make an enquiry feel like a sensible next step, not a sales shortcut. On mobile, service choices and contact actions had to remain easy to follow. The portfolio story needed to reflect that technical decision process while avoiding promises about energy use, comfort gains or installation results that depend on the property and system.
fields.description_2:
I organised Kervana around the type of question a homeowner is likely to bring to the site. Heating, climate solutions and maintenance each have a clear route, with supporting information introduced after the visitor has chosen the area that fits the situation. This keeps technical detail useful instead of overwhelming the first screen.

Enquiry actions appear where someone has enough context to explain the property or system. I kept headings direct and the wording plain so visitors do not need specialist knowledge before making contact. On smaller screens, service cards, practical details and next steps keep the same order. The portfolio case now explains Kervana as a technical service journey, without claiming guaranteed savings, comfort levels or installation outcomes.

fields.description_1:
Envolt combines electrical work with energy solutions, so visitors can arrive with different starting points. One person may need an electrical installation, while another is exploring charging or energy-related improvements. Treating every service as one generic technical offer would make it harder to understand what belongs together and what needs separate advice.

The website therefore needed clear service routes, enough project context to show the type of work involved and an obvious way to request advice. Technical claims also had to stay measured because performance, capacity and suitability depend on the property and installation. On mobile, the same choices needed to remain visible without long blocks of engineering language. The portfolio problem was to make a broad technical offer easy to navigate without oversimplifying it.
fields.description_2:
I structured Envolt around separate technical needs instead of one long list of capabilities. Electrical work, energy solutions and related project information each have their own place, so visitors can start with the question they recognise and then read the details that matter for that route. Project examples support understanding without acting as guarantees for future work.

Advice and quotation actions sit close to the service information rather than being repeated without context. I used short headings and plain explanations to keep the site readable for non-specialists. On mobile, service choices, project content and contact actions keep a clear sequence. The portfolio case now reflects Envolt's real multi-service technical offer while avoiding unsupported claims about savings, performance, payback or installation speed.

fields.description_1:
Ozturkmotionpictures has to win trust through creative work, but couples still need practical information before choosing a wedding filmmaker. A showreel communicates style, but it does not explain what is included, how the service works or how someone can make contact. The website therefore needed to balance emotion and practical decision-making instead of relying only on visual impact.

Film examples had to remain central while service information and enquiry routes stayed easy to find. On mobile, large media blocks could not push useful details too far down. The portfolio story also needed to avoid vague claims about unforgettable results or customer reactions. The real challenge was to let the work speak for itself while giving couples a clear route from inspiration to a relevant enquiry.
fields.description_2:
I placed Ozturkmotionpictures' film work at the centre of the WordPress experience, then added service context around the moments when a couple is likely to ask practical questions. Wedding films and visual examples establish the creative direction first, while concise explanations clarify the offer without interrupting the viewing experience.

Enquiry actions appear after enough work and context have been shown to make the conversation meaningful. On smaller screens, media, text and calls to action follow a simple order so the portfolio does not become a long wall of video. I kept the case description focused on presentation and decision flow rather than subjective promises. It now explains how the site connects creative proof with an understandable path to contact.

fields.description_1:
Odetra presents property investment opportunities, where visitors need more than an attractive project image before deciding whether to ask for details. Investors need to understand the opportunity, project context and relevant information before they are ready for contact. If promotional language appears before that context, the offer can feel less credible and harder to evaluate.

The website therefore needed a clear order from opportunity overview to project detail and enquiry. Investment wording also had to stay careful because returns, value growth and suitability cannot be assumed from page design or general project information. On mobile, cards and project details needed to remain readable. The portfolio challenge was to present investment-oriented property information clearly without turning the case study into financial promotion or inventing performance outcomes.
fields.description_2:
I organised Odetra so each property opportunity can be understood through its own project context before a visitor reaches the enquiry step. The WordPress structure separates the overview from deeper information, allowing investors to scan available projects first and then focus on the details that are relevant to a specific opportunity.

Contact actions remain visible after the supporting information instead of replacing it. I kept investment language factual and avoided claims about returns, appreciation or suitability that require separate financial evidence. On mobile, project cards, supporting details and enquiry actions keep the same priority. The portfolio case now explains the information architecture behind the investment presentation and shows how the site supports a considered next step without promising commercial or financial results.

fields.description_1:
Marcoverhuurt needs to help renters move from a practical job or event need to the right rental item. Visitors may not know the product name, so a catalogue organised around internal item names can make discovery harder. They also need the conditions, details and a way to request or reserve equipment before committing.

The website therefore needed clear rental categories, scannable item information and a next step without assuming every product has the same availability or terms. Mobile browsing matters because customers may search while preparing work on location. The portfolio story had to stay specific to the rental journey and avoid promises about stock or availability that change over time. The challenge was to make equipment discovery practical without oversimplifying the conditions around rental.
fields.description_2:
I structured Marcoverhuurt around the way a renter searches for equipment rather than around a flat inventory. Clear categories provide the first route, and each item can then show the practical details needed before someone asks about availability or continues with a reservation or enquiry. This keeps product information close to the decision it supports.

I avoided wording that suggests every item is always available or that rental conditions never change. On smaller screens, category links, item cards and next-step actions follow a compact order so browsing remains manageable in the field. The portfolio case now describes a real rental workflow: identify the need, inspect the relevant item information and continue with the appropriate request, without generic ecommerce claims or invented operational results.
